item.description: 🗓 On October 15, the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly adopted a resolution entitled “Addressing Contemporary Forms of Colonialism” . The draft was prepared by the Group of Friends in Defence of the UN Charter , with Russia’s active participation. 19 states co-sponsored the resolution . 🌐 The resolution is non-confrontational and unifying in nature. It stresses the need to eradicate neocolonial practices , including interference in internal affairs, unilateral coercive measures, the imposition of unfair international treaties and restrictions on technological development. These practices are among the most serious obstacles to achieving the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and are a root cause of numerous problems on the UN agenda. ✅ The document was supported by 85 Member States, with 49 voting against and 23 abstaining. item.title: 🇷🇺 On October 16, President of Russia Vladimir Putin and Pope Leo XIV had a telephone conversation
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇻🇦 📞 On October 16, President of Russia Vladimir Putin and Pope Leo XIV had a telephone conversation . After wishing the supreme pontiff sound health and a speedy recovery after the surgery he had undergone recently, Vladimir Putin emphasised the importance of the cooperation between Russia and the Vatican in promoting common moral values and protecting Christians and Christian shrines across the world . Both Sides reaffirmed their interest in maintaining dialogue between the Russian Orthodox Church and the Catholic Church. During an exchange of views on the situation surrounding Ukraine, Vladimir Putin thanked the Pope for his willingness to contribute to resolving the conflict and his humanitarian efforts . In response to the Pontiff’s concern for civilians in the Russian city of Alyoshki , Kherson Region, comprehensive explanations were provided regarding the Kiev regime’s responsibility for the difficult humanitarian situation there. Support was expressed for the Vatican’s intention to help create conditions to ensure the safety of the city’s population and arrange deliveries of vital supplies. It was agreed to cooperate on this matter. Support was expressed for the Vatican's intention to facilitate creating the necessary conditions to keep the town's population safe and beginning vital supplies . The two Sides agreed to cooperate in this regard. The conversation was constructive and mutually respectful.

🎙
Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman
Maria Zakharova
’s
answer to a media question
regarding
Poland’s plans concerning the Kaliningrad Region
(October 16, 2026)
❓
Question: In a recent interview with the Italian newspaper La Repubblica, Chair of the NATO Military Committee Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone said that the North Atlantic Alliance had no plans to blockade Kaliningrad. “I want to be absolutely clear: NATO is not preparing any blockade of Kaliningrad. This is a threat built around a scenario that does not exist,” he emphasised. How would you comment on this?
Maria Zakharova:
Yes, such a statement was indeed made. Let us assume, difficult as it may be to believe, that the Admiral is being sincere this time. If so, what plans are actually being drawn up?
For example, on October 12, at the annual Warsaw Security Forum, one of the central events was a keynote address by NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus Grynkewich, entitled Theory of Victory: How Do We Achieve Military Success Against Russia in Deterrence and Defence?
A senior NATO general chose Warsaw, t
he capital of a country currently pursuing militarisation at a breakneck pace
, to present his proposals, the analytical merits of which we shall leave you to judge. It is worth noting that Poland harbours ambitions to turn its Wojsko Polskie into perhaps the most powerful military in Europe, and specific scenarios for its deployment are already being drawn up.
For instance, the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces has developed operational plans for launching
pre-emptive precision strikes against the Kaliningrad Region
, should a “war with Russia become inevitable”. Just consider this: nothing has happened yet, but the Polish hussars are already charging ahead in formation.
Specifically, the plan envisages the destruction of all military infrastructure, primarily Iskander and S-400 missile systems, as well as ammunition depots, fuel terminals and command posts. The operation would involve US-made HIMARS and Polish Homar-K missile systems with a range of up to 300 kilometres, F-16 fighter jets armed with precision-guided missiles with a range of up to 1,000 kilometres, loitering munitions and combat UAVs.
At the same time, Polish coastal anti-ship missile systems and NATO aircraft would be used to i
mpose a naval blockade on the Kaliningrad Region
. The aim would be to prevent Baltic Fleet vessels from leaving their bases and to cut off the region’s supply routes. In parallel, a ground offensive in the Suwałki Gap is envisaged, involving the 16th and 18th Mechanised Divisions and the 1st Infantry Division of the Polish Armed Forces.
Is this not essentially Operation Barbarossa 2.0?
❗️
However, the “strategists” in Warsaw and elsewhere would do well to remember what President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
and Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov
have
repeatedly stated
:
any treacherous armed attack against the Kaliningrad Region
will be met with a literally incinerating response
, using every means at Russia’s disposal.
The war will be very short.

item.title: 🗓 On October 15-16, a CSTO, CIS and SCO Conference on Security in Central Asia and Afghanistan
item.description: 🗓 On October 15-16, a CSTO, CIS and SCO Conference on Security in Central Asia and Afghanistan was held in Moscow as part of Russia’s CSTO chairmanship programme. Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov presented Russia’s latest assessments of the state of affairs in the region, emphasising Russia’s unwavering commitment to strengthening allied ties with its partners and preserving Central Asia as a region of peace and prosperity . Special emphasis was placed on the need to implement the initiative to establish new architecture of equal and indivisible security in Eurasia , which would help stabilise the situation across the continent over the long term. The plenary session was attended by Deputy Speaker of the Federation Council Konstantin Kosachev ; Deputy Secretary of the Security Council of the Russian Federation Alexey Shevtsov ; the heads of the #CSTO , #CIS , and #SCO executive bodies; and heads of several diplomatic missions. The discussions covered a broad range of issues involving the developments in the region , including the situation in Afghanistan. The participants expressed a shared view on the importance of coordinating their approaches , stepping up cooperation within existing regional and international frameworks, and developing practical proposals to respond effectively to modern-day challenges and threats. The efforts undertaken by the CSTO, the CIS, and the SCO to maintain stability were highly praised .

item.title: 🇷🇺 On October 16, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met with Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇷🇸 On October 16, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met with Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia Ivica Dačić in Moscow. The Parties discussed the current state of the Russian-Serbian cooperation and its future prospects across key areas. Regarding international issues, particular emphasis was placed on the situation in the Balkans . The Ministers underscored the fundamental importance of UN Security Council Resolution 1244 for the settlement of the Kosovo problem , as well as their mutual interest in maintaining stability in the region.

The UN’s excessively permissive attitude towards the existence of
an entire network of “secret prisons”
for POWs in Kiev-controlled territory
encourages the spread of this criminal practice
and disregard for the provisions of the relevant UN Convention.
Hundreds of Russian servicemen we have interviewed,
who endured the hell of Ukrainian prison camps
, consistently describe a
n entire network of facilities holding POWs
. Several reports by foreign human rights defenders refer to them in highly evasive terms as
“transit prisons”
, where servicemen are held during the initial stages of captivity.
In these cramped stone cells, underground dungeons and cages, generally located on the premises of Ukrainian military units and nationalist battalions,
everything human is subjected to utter degradation – from personal dignity to life itself.
Militants who conceal their faces behind masks and balaclavas and address one another by call signs
subject captured Russian servicemen to inhuman abuse.
❗️
Simulated drowning, “electric chairs”, dog attacks and amputations without anaesthesia are just a fraction of the methods systematically employed there by Ukrainian punitive forces.
***
The Kiev authorities deny human rights defenders and observers access to these
torture chambers
. Yet we have collected
hundreds of accounts
of what happens there and have repeatedly submitted them to the UN Secretariat. I am certain that conscientious, impartial human rights defenders could obtain this information with even a minimal willingness to do so.
We know for a fact that such
“prisons”
exist in the
Kharkov, Dnepropetrovsk and Sumy regions
, and even
in Kiev
.
In this connection,
I have just one question
: what will it take for the UN Committee against Torture to make it a priority to investigate Ukraine’s well-known yet persistently ignored system of
“secret prisons”
?
Many experts are aware of this shameful phenomenon.
What is lacking is the political will to overcome pressure from foreign parties complicit in the conflict
, who shield the Kiev regime from accountability and detailed investigations into its actions.
👉
I hope the Committee will take these remarks into account and finally address this unacceptable practice in order to put an end to it once and for all.
#KievRegimeCrimes

🎙
Statement
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the Plenary Session of the
#CSTO
,
#CIS
and
#SCO
Conference on Security in Central Asia and Afghanistan
(
Moscow, October 16, 2026
)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
Everyone has an interest in ensuring that
Central Asia remains a region of peace & prosperity
, underpinned by broad, mutually beneficial cooperation among all the states in the region and, of course, their immediate neighbours.
For Russia, this region holds particular strategic significance
: geographical, historical and humanitarian factors mean that important Russian interests are concentrated here.
☝️
We see one way of safeguarding these interests in
maintaining relations of alliance and strategic partnership on an equal footing with all Central Asian countries,
helping them ensure
peaceful and secure development
both bilaterally and through the integration mechanisms operating in the region.
We assess the situation in Central Asia as stable and conducive to international cooperation
, despite the well-known risks. We appreciate
the enormous contribution
made by the region’s Leaders to creating all the necessary conditions for this.
At the same time,
we must not lose sight of the risks we all know about
, which arise primarily from the actions of certain external players seeking to pursue their narrow, self-serving geopolitical objectives without regard for the region’s specific circumstances or the interests of the friendly peoples of Central Asia.
Today, especially before this audience, there is no need to convince anyone that
the countries of the “collective West” have been trying for many years to create flashpoints along our borders
. In particular, their role in
deliberately engineering the Ukrainian crisis
is well known – through years of
relentless eastward NATO expansion towards Russia’s borders
, as well as through unqualified support for the openly neo-Nazi, Russophobic Kiev regime, which is once again showing its true colours in these very days.
❗️
In this connection,
I would emphasise that
absolutely any country in the world
, including our partners in Central Asia,
could fall victim to the West’s geopolitical expansion and the “colour revolutions” it orchestrates.
Such attempts have already been made against a number of our neighbours, but were successfully thwarted.
***
Developments in Afghanistan could still adversely affect regional security
, especially if unscrupulous external players exploit them for short-term interests that have nothing in common with those of Central Asian countries and Russia.
We strive to be realistic and, in this regard, understand that overcoming
the grim legacy
left by the US and other NATO countries after two decades of inglorious occupation of Afghanistan will take a long time.
👉
We proceed from the understanding that the Taliban government is a reality that must be reckoned with.
A growing number of countries are coming to recognise this. On the political front, we are working to consolidate external support for the authorities in Kabul and those aspects of their work that objectively serve the interests of regional security.
Russia fully shares the vision of Afghanistan as an independent, united and peaceful state, free from war and drugs.
We regard as an important success the fact that
the latest meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan
, held in Moscow in early October, reaffirmed the participating countries’ rejection of a confrontational approach towards Kabul.

item.title: 🗓 On October 15, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov took part in the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia
item.description: 🗓 On October 15, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov took part in the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia ( #CICA ) in Baku. 👉 Sergey Lavrov's opening remarks at the Summit's Plenary Session Discussions focused on prospects for CICA’s development and its adaptation to the changing international environment. The Russian Side emphasised the importance of integrating CICA harmoniously into the emerging architecture of cooperation across Eurasia , with a view to establishing a continent-wide framework of equal and indivisible security and seamless cross-border socioeconomic connectivity. 🤝 Sergey Lavrov reaffirmed Russia’s unwavering commitment to deepening practical cooperation within CICA , including in the areas it coordinates : international information security and support for small and medium-sized enterprises. Other priorities include fostering contacts between volunteer organisations and advancing mechanisms for practical industrial cooperation. Our country’s contribution to strengthening transport and logistics links across the CICA region was also highlighted. Russia welcomed the extension of Azerbaijan’s CICA chairmanship for 2027-2028 and supported Laos joining the Conference as a full member.
